name: reviewbot-pr-identity-pause
description:
A signed pull_request webhook, posted to the production route: the pipeline mints a session and binds the pull request into the class's github_pull_request/write_memory slot at session mint (fillFrom: [trigger]) — no human, no approval, only the verified delivery. The session reads the pull request with `gh pr view`, and the toolspec's two requireSlotBound writesRelationships blocks write the author/repo identity tuples for it; both land, because the resource they name is the SAME pull request the delivery bound. It then reads a SECOND pull request the delivery never named: the same two blocks match the call, but the slot-bound checker finds no grant for THAT resource, and relwrites.ErrSlotBoundRefused flips the tool result to IsError with the gate's own text. One call succeeds, the identically-shaped next one is refused, and the only difference is which resource the trigger bound — that contrast is what proves the gate discriminates rather than always allowing (or always denying).

Every assertion below reads a TOOL RESULT, never a reply: nothing in the transcript calls respond_to_user. The fixture still carries a SECOND Channel (kind=fake, role=output) alongside the github input, and that pairing is not optional narrative — github's ValidateSpec rejects role=output|both, and the pipeline's session-create path refuses to mint a session at all for a role=input Channel whose class resolves no role=output Channel, independent of whether a reply is ever sent. See task-6-report.md for why a Slack-REPLY loop is still not expressible here regardless: userTurns and trigger are mutually exclusive at the loader (pkg/bronzethread/bundle.go, Bundle.Validate), so a triggered run cannot express a later human inbound of any kind, on any channel — the output Channel this fixture carries is a one-way destination, never a source.

No record_observation (pool-write) leg: task-6-report.md documents why — the in-process harness's Loop.Mem never reaches pkg/memory/httpsrv, which is the ONLY place the pool-write authorization gate (destinationFor, gated on pools.ForSession(...).Write) is implemented; *memory.Local itself has no PutToPool method at all. Exercising that leg for real needs an in-process httpsrv + httpclient.Client wired into the shared harness, which is out of this task's scope.

No trace.golden yet — per AGENTS.md, a golden is promoted only after the property assertions here have proven the scenario; that promotion is left to a later pass.

args.description: read the triggering pull request and record identity relationships about it

args._reason: read the pull request the delivery bound, to record who authored it and where it lives
check a second pull request this session was never triggered for

expect.lastToolResultContains: has no slot-bound grant for this session

args.summary: Recorded author/repo identity for demo-org/demo-repo#7; a second, untriggered pull request was correctly refused.
